START WITH A QUESTION

You have probably wondered.

The short answers are here. The experiments let you inspect the evidence yourself.

01

Can a website know I copied something?

It can receive a copy event when you copy from its page. That does not automatically give it your entire clipboard, or copies made in other apps.

02

Can it detect screenshots?

There is no universal web event confirming an operating-system screenshot. Some shortcuts or an explicitly permitted clipboard read can provide clues.

03

Can it see my other tabs or apps?

It can often observe that its own page lost focus or became hidden. That does not reveal which tab or app you opened, or what you did there.

04

Can it see my IP address and location?

The server sees the address of the connection reaching it. An IP database may estimate a location; it can be wrong and is separate from permission-based device location.

05

Can it recognise my browser?

Browser and rendering characteristics can be combined into a fingerprint. It can help group visits, but is changeable, can be shared, and does not prove who you are.

06

Can it detect my Chrome extensions?

Some extensions expose resource references or page changes. A page cannot reliably list every installed extension or prove that an extension is working.

THREE STEPS, NO SPECIAL KNOWLEDGE

How it works

Every experiment separates the action you try, the signal this browser sends, and the things that signal cannot establish.

  1. 1

    Start with ordinary page signals.

    The lab shows browser-reported values and events from its own page. Entering does not start protected camera, microphone, clipboard or location experiments.

  2. 2

    Try something and inspect the result.

    Copy the sample, click a button, or switch tabs and return. No matching event does not prove that an action did not happen.

  3. 3

    Choose whether to explore further.

    Open Permission lab for individual access requests, or use Expert mode for technical readings. Expert mode changes the display; it grants no extra permissions.

KNOW WHAT THIS LAB KEEPS

Your data, explained.

Live readings stay in this page's memory. Optional JSON exports are saved to your device. This demo does not upload camera, screen, audio or clipboard payloads.

This host privately counts page entries and estimates visits without cookies. It uses temporary daily request signatures; hosting access logs may also exist.

Read the full privacy details

A separate same-origin entry request counts page views and estimates visits using a salted HMAC of the connection IP and bounded user-agent. The counter does not retain raw IP addresses or user-agents. Its signature map is replaced on the first counted request of a new UTC day. Aggregate daily counts remain for 90 days; lifetime totals remain. These estimates do not count unique people. Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track opts out of the counter.

The connection check receives ordinary request metadata and uses this host's offline IP-location database. It does not silently request device location. IP location can be wrong or identify a VPN or proxy exit. Hosting access logs are separate from this demo.

Permission readings can be personal. An export may contain your connection address, browser details, location or selected-device metadata. It contains no typed text, clipboard payload, credentials or raw media. Imported comparison files are read in this browser and are not uploaded.

Ending a session clears its page memory and stops active demos. Browser grants and downloaded files remain under your control. There are no visitor accounts, third-party advertising pixels or third-party analytics services.

01 / COPYINGPage events

Does this page notice copying?

It can receive copy, cut and paste events in its document. That alone does not read your system clipboard.

Select and copy this sentence. A copy event can be observed without reading what is on your clipboard.

Select the sample, then use your usual Copy command.

What this page observed

No matching event observed yet.

Copies in another app are not delivered here. Reading clipboard contents is a separate, explicit experiment in Permission lab.

02 / CLICKSPage events

What does a click reveal?

A page can receive a click's position and element type. It can also read text entered into its own fields; this demo discards typed text.

What this page observed

No matching event observed yet.

A browser-dispatched event is not proof of physical human input. Scripts can also generate synthetic events, shown separately in Expert mode.

03 / TABS AND FOCUSPage state

Does it know when I leave?

The browser can report that this page lost focus or became hidden. It does not report your destination.

Open a test tab ↗

Switch to another tab, then return here.

What this page observed

No matching event observed yet.

Browser controls, permission prompts, another app or minimising a window can also affect focus. Their contents are not exposed.

04 / SCREENSHOTSPossible clues

Will it notice a screenshot?

There is no universal event confirming an operating-system screenshot. A shortcut only becomes a clue if it reaches this page.

Try your usual screenshot shortcut

On Windows, try Print Screen or Windows + Shift + S. On macOS, try Command + Shift + 3 or 4. On a phone, use its screenshot controls. Return to inspect any signal this browser delivered.

What this page observed

No matching event observed yet.

No clue does not prove that no screenshot happened. A clipboard image, if explicitly read, could also be a copied picture.

      YOU CHOOSE THE EXTRA ACCESS

      Permission lab

      Switching off releases a demo's resources. It does not revoke saved browser grants or erase earlier readings. One-off snapshots are historical results, not continuous monitoring.
      RECOGNITION HAS LIMITS

      A fingerprint is a combination.

      A site can combine browser characteristics to help group visits. Similar systems can match, and the same system can change. A match does not establish identity.

      Several readings. One summary.

      Browser settingsScreen detailsRendering samples→Summary hash

      Hashing does not create a verified identity. This demo does not use these signatures to track you across websites or measure population uniqueness.

      WebGL extensions are graphics capabilities, not installed browser extensions. Window size differs from screen dimensions; a simple window resize does not necessarily change the fingerprint.

      A CONTROLLED COMPARISON

      Compare browser snapshots.

      Useful for testing a privacy extension or browser setting. Matching values do not prove a protection failed; differences do not identify their cause.

      1. Capture and export a baseline.
      2. Change one extension or browser setting.
      3. Reload if required, then import the baseline.
      4. Compare with current readings and inspect the differences.

      Keep both snapshots on your device.

      Import an Observatory JSON export. Size and structure are checked, and values are rendered as text. Your file is read in this browser, not uploaded.

      Import a baseline or capture the current session to begin.

      Browser updates, screen settings, permissions, randomisation and timing can also change readings. Unavailable and unstable values need careful interpretation. No unique-person or extension-success score is calculated.

      These are explanatory limits, separate from successful observations. A missing signal can have several causes.
